IR.rationale: A rising 5Y-Fed Funds spread signals a repricing of the expected policy path. Higher discount rates and tighter expected policy tend to weigh on equity valuations over the following weeks.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark a credit sell-off that raises the risk premium. Higher compensation for risk tends to precede higher subsequent equity returns.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility embeds a high variance and equity risk premium. This predicts higher subsequent returns as fear subsides.

AP.rationale: At weekly horizons broad market moves partially reverse through liquidity provision and overreaction. A strong market week therefore says something about the next weeks' sector returns.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of conservative-investment firms reflects a defensive tilt. Such tilts tend to occur when required returns are elevated.

FX.rationale: AUD is a pro-cyclical risk-on currency. Its recent strength summarises global growth and risk appetite relevant for cyclical sectors.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity strength captures global demand and inflation news. This matters for the cash flows of energy, materials and industrial sectors and for the input costs of consumer sectors.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reduce credit availability and risk-bearing capacity. This shifts expected equity returns over short horizons.

ENDG.rationale: Sector returns show short-horizon reversal. A strong recent run tends to be followed by weaker returns.

IR.rationale: Abrupt term-spread changes reflect shocks to the policy and growth outlook. Such shocks feed into equity uncertainty beyond what past variance captures.

B.rationale: Falling high-yield prices with widening spreads signal rising default risk and leverage. Through the leverage and credit channel this raises future equity volatility.

V.rationale: Implied volatility is a forward-looking variance forecast. When equity and oil uncertainty are both elevated, the risk is broad-based and more persistent.

AP.rationale: Joint weakness in US and EM equities signals a global risk-off episode. Via the leverage effect and volatility feedback, negative returns predict higher subsequent volatility.

ST.rationale: Flight to quality toward profitable firms tends to accompany deteriorating conditions. Such periods are followed by higher realised volatility.

FX.rationale: A broad dollar rally together with yen appreciation is the classic safe-haven, funding-unwind state. It precedes turbulent equity markets.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs signal weakening global demand and stress in commodity-linked sectors. Both raise future equity variance.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions constrain intermediaries' risk-bearing capacity. This amplifies price swings and raises realised volatility.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters but mean-reverts. An unusually high recent variance relative to history carries information beyond the baseline persistence.

IR.rationale: Rate changes have no robust mechanism or consistent relation to left-tail sector outcomes at these horizons, so the group is left empty.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads signal rising default risk. That deterioration can spill into equity drawdowns.

V.rationale: High implied volatility across equity and oil widens the return distribution. This raises the probability of extreme losses.

AP.rationale: Small-cap underperformance signals deteriorating risk appetite and liquidity. Such states precede equity drawdowns.

ST.rationale: Crowded momentum gains raise the risk of sharp unwinds and momentum crashes. These coincide with sector losses.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects carry-trade unwinding and safe-haven demand. Both are associated with equity tail risk.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps hit energy and related sectors directly. They can also signal weakening global demand.

MC.rationale: Simultaneously tight financial conditions and elevated stress identify systemic strain. In such states fire sales and deleveraging produce large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns raise volatility through the leverage effect. They can also start a drawdown that continues, widening the left tail.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates ease discount rates. They often accompany anticipated policy support, which can trigger strong rallies.

B.rationale: After high-yield sell-offs, elevated risk premia and wider distributions make sharp equity rebounds more likely.

V.rationale: High implied volatility and policy uncertainty widen the return distribution. Resolution of the uncertainty produces large relief rallies.

AP.rationale: Weak market weeks are followed by reversals and by higher volatility. Both raise the chance of an extreme positive return.

ST.rationale: Defensive, conservative-investment leadership marks risk-averse periods with elevated premia. Such periods precede strong rebounds.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength reflects global risk aversion and tighter dollar funding. Its reversal is associated with sharp risk-asset rallies.

COM.rationale: Commodity slumps depress cyclical and energy sectors. Their oversold state sets up large rebounds when demand fears ease.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress widens both tails. Stress relief brings outsized gains.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent sector returns lead to reversal and higher volatility. Both increase the probability of a large gain.
